source.title: Channel Location Constrains the Auditability of Subliminal Learning

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It reports its own measurements of cross-model unembedding-neighbour geometry and an anchor-supervised cross-tokenizer alignment. These bear conceptually on representational convergence and mapping, but use different objects and measures from the original claim.
record.gate_note: The paper measures convergence of output-token neighbourhood geometry and tests an anchor-supervised map between output bases. Its scale sweep measures subliminal-transfer leakage, not representational alignment, so those leakage values are not recorded as scale-convergence results. Cited representational-universality findings are not treated as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The paper is about subliminal learning, but it reports its own measurements of cross-model convergence: overlap of unembedding-neighbour sets between independently trained bases. It also fits an anchor-supervised orthogonal map between two models' output bases. These are new objects and measures (output-token neighbourhood geometry, not the representations of paired inputs), so this is a new setting with results on convergence and mappability, not a replication of the original method.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly wrong. The authors say unembedding-neighbour geometry converges across independently trained runs, which they call a facet of representational universality. They say this convergence explains why masked token traits transfer regardless of initialization. They describe cross-tokenizer alignment as approximate, not exact: 'alignable but not perfectly isometric.' They do not state that this is not evidence for alignment increasing with scale; that caveat is the reader's own.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines unembedding-neighbour geometry and an anchor-supervised output-basis map, rather than reproducing the original representation-similarity measurement or its scale/performance analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The cross-tokenizer result depends on anchor-supervised orthogonal alignment; a scrambled-anchor control is at the floor, and a more flexible ridge map performs worse. Neighbour overlap is measured for top-40 neighbours in the Pythia pair; the RedPajama comparison reports a mean over 12 traits.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 53 tokens, more convergent neighbourhoods (higher cross-base Jaccard) predict smaller shared-minus-different-base transfer gaps (Spearman −0.44, [−0.65, −0.17]). The shared neighbour core is about 0.1 higher in cosine to the target token than the base-specific remainder.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The degree of cross-model convergence of output geometry predicts initialization-independent transfer of distilled traits.

record.problems: The convergence evidence covers few model pairs and does not establish a scale trend. The cross-tokenizer alignment is anchor-supervised and recovers only part of within-tokenizer transfer. The paper notes that some cross-family comparisons jointly vary data, architecture, and scale.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many subliminal-transfer, screening, and mitigation outcomes, including leakage trends across model sizes. They do not measure representational alignment or similarity and were therefore not included. Cited convergence results from other work were also excluded.

untested.parts: Whether alignment increases with model size or capability. Only one cross-architecture pair is measured, and the scale sweep measures leakage, not alignment. Alignment of representations of the same inputs is not measured either.
Unit- or basis-level matching and internal-layer features. Only output-row neighbourhoods are compared, in a single seed pair.
Internal-representation maps, stitching, relative representations, and maps without paired anchors. Only an anchor-supervised output-basis map is tested, on 8 token pairs.
Entirely untested. No sensitivity of the Jaccard result to neighbour count or similarity measure is reported.
The causes of convergence are not isolated. The authors assert convergence 'across models trained on similar data' without testing it.

missing.what: Spearman 0.67 between full neighbour-similarity vectors across the Pythia and deduped bases; it appears only as a note in R1 and should be its own row.
missing.locator: Section 4.2; Appendix A 'Convergence and supporting real-LM results'

missing.what: Controls for the cross-tokenizer map: scrambled anchors fall to the naive floor; the map recovers 4× a minimal centroid stitch; the ridge map does worse. These are noted but not recorded as rows.

record.verdict_notes: The study's main subject is subliminal learning; the convergence results are supporting evidence for its explanation of initialization-independent transfer. The scale sweep (leakage rising with size in Pythia) measures trait leakage, not alignment, and is correctly excluded. Huh et al. (Platonic Representation Hypothesis) is cited as reference 44, but this study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether alignment increases as model size or capability increases, or compare distances between representations of the same input data across models. It tests output-token neighbourhood geometry in a small number of model pairs.
The tested map is anchor-supervised and concerns output-basis geometry, not general internal representations, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired anchors.
The study does not isolate shared data or objectives from other causes of cross-model geometric convergence.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M and Pythia-410M-deduped
rows.operation_detail: Compared unembedding-neighbour geometry across independently trained bases.
rows.measure: Mean Jaccard overlap of top-40 unembedding neighbours
rows.note: The paper also reports that full neighbour-similarity vectors correlate at Spearman 0.67; the shared-neighbour core is about 0.1 higher in cosine to the target token than the base-specific remainder.
rows.check: Wrongly linked to V1. Pythia-410M and Pythia-410M-deduped share architecture and size; Table 5 calls the pair a 'same data, new seed' reseed, though deduplication changes the data slightly. So the row bears on convergence across seeds (V3), not cross-architecture convergence with scale (V1). Jaccard 0.66 against a 0.00 random baseline is shared neighbourhood structure without identical rows, which fits V3.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, text preceding Figure 6 and Figure 6 caption.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M and RedPajama-INCITE-3B
rows.operation_detail: Compared target-token unembedding-neighbour sets across bases.
rows.note: The models differ in data, seed, architecture, and scale but share the GPT-NeoX tokenizer; the study presents this as robustness evidence, not an isolated causal test of any one difference.
rows.check: This is one cross-architecture, cross-data pair (Pythia-410M vs RedPajama-3B, shared tokenizer). It shows cross-model alignment of neighbourhood geometry but cannot show the increase with scale that V1 names. The neighbour count is not stated for this comparison (top-40 is stated only for the Pythia pair). The 0.00 random baseline is reported for the Pythia pair, not this one.

source_check.correct: Jaccard overlap is 0.68 over twelve traits. For V1, state=cannot_determine: this single cross-model comparison does not measure increasing alignment with scale or capability.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, independent-base comparison and Figure 6 caption.
source_check.problem: Cross-model overlap alone cannot establish V1's scale-dependent increase.

rows.subject: Pythia teacher and Qwen2.5-3B student
rows.size_stated: Pythia size not stated for this experiment; Qwen2.5-3B
rows.operation_detail: Fit an orthogonal alignment on byte-identical anchor tokens and routed the Pythia teacher's token-neighbour signal into the Qwen vocabulary.

conditions.value: byte-identical single-token anchors; target and neighbours excluded

rows.baseline: Within-tokenizer transfer rate; numeric value not stated
rows.note: The study says the alignment is anchor-supervised and establishes carrier identity rather than spontaneous cross-tokenizer transfer. Scrambled anchors sit at the naive floor; a more flexible ridge map performs worse.
rows.check: The measure is recovered subliminal-transfer fraction after routing through a Procrustes map fit on byte-identical anchors, an indirect gauge of mapping loss. Mean 0.41 (range 0.17–0.74) is a clearly incomplete recovery. The authors say the bases are 'alignable but not perfectly isometric'. The locator is Appendix A 'Cross-tokenizer substitution', referenced from Section 4.2.

relationships.reason: Neighbour sets overlap with Jaccard 0.66 against 0.00 for a random baseline, and similarity vectors correlate at Spearman 0.67: shared structure without identical rows (R1).
relationships.display_finding: Neighbour sets had Jaccard overlap of 0.66 versus 0.00 for a random baseline, and similarity vectors had Spearman correlation of 0.67.
